title: California's 38th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for California's 38th Congressional District is an open-seat race following mid-decade redistricting under Proposition 50, which led incumbent Representative Linda Sánchez to run in a different nearby district. The district spans parts of Los Angeles and Orange Counties, including communities such as El Monte, Montebello, La Habra Heights, and Yorba Linda, with a voter registration of roughly 45% Democratic, 24% Republican, and 25% no party preference. Democratic nominee Hilda Solis, a former U.S. Representative and U.S. Secretary of Labor who currently serves on the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors, faces Republican nominee Pedro Casas, a retired U.S. Army Colonel and clinical psychologist. Cook Political Report rates the general election as Solidly Democratic, though Casas is campaigning on public safety, border security, and economic issues.
polling_note: No independent general election polls were found for this race as of mid-June 2026. Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Democratic.

candidates.name: Hilda Solis
candidates.summary: Hilda Solis is a Democrat and current Los Angeles County Supervisor for the 1st District, a position she has held since 2014. She previously served as the 25th U.S. Secretary of Labor under President Barack Obama from 2009 to 2013 and as a U.S. Representative for California's 31st and 32nd congressional districts from 2001 to 2009. Her campaign emphasizes environmental justice, affordable housing, healthcare access, workers' rights, and opposition to the Trump administration's policies.

candidates.name: Pedro Casas
candidates.summary: Pedro 'Antonio' Casas is a Republican candidate and a retired U.S. Army Colonel with 29 years of military service, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan where he commanded medical detachments. He is a clinical, forensic, and aero-medical psychologist with a Ph.D. in Counseling Psychology from UC Santa Barbara, and his campaign platform emphasizes border security, public safety, education reform through JROTC programs, tax cuts, and combating the fentanyl crisis. Casas was born in El Paso, Texas, grew up in Baldwin Park, California, and has no previous elected political experience.
